The four directions of the First Nations Mental Wellness Continuum, from published indicators

Source: R/indigenous_frameworks.R
mhcont.Rd

Lays out a group's published indicators under the four outcomes of the First Nations Mental Wellness Continuum Framework (hope, belonging, meaning, purpose), each with its interval, and says which directions the tables have no measure of.

Usage

mhcont(
  data,
  grp,
  ind,
  est,
  lower,
  upper,
  hope = NULL,
  belong = NULL,
  meaning = NULL,
  purp = NULL,
  qual = NULL,
  conflvl = 0.95
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per group and indicator.

grp, ind, est, lower, upper

Column names: the group, the indicator, the estimate (percent) and its published limits.

hope, belong, meaning, purp

The indicators taken as proxies for each direction, or NULL where the tables have none.

qual

Optional column of quality flags: "E" rows are marked use with caution, and suppressed ones ("F", "x", "..") get no estimate.

conflvl

Confidence level of the published intervals (default 0.95).

Value

A data frame with the classes rmbl_wellness_continuum and rmbl_wellness_profile. Its columns are group, indicator (the direction), side ("wellness"), domain (the proxies), estimate, lower, upper, usewithcau, shared, proxy (always TRUE).

Details

The Framework (Health Canada and Assembly of First Nations 2015) describes mental wellness as hope for the future, a sense of belonging and connectedness to family, community and culture, a sense of meaning and of how one's life fits into creation, and purpose in daily life. It has no numeric scoring, and no survey table measures the four directions as the Framework defines them. This function takes the indicators a user names as proxies for each (hope = "Always or often has a hopeful outlook", ...), reports each direction's level (the mean of its proxies, their standard errors combined as independent; the proxies share respondents, so if they are positively correlated that standard error is too small), marks every row as a proxy, and reports a direction given no proxy as missing rather than filling it from another. One indicator named for two directions (Statistics Canada asks about “meaning and purpose” together) is used for both and marked shared.

The result plots as a welprof. For the balance across the directions, call holbal on the rows with a proxy (x[x$domain != "no published proxy", ], with "domain" as its domain column): a missing direction otherwise leaves the balance NA, and a shared proxy counts once per direction it serves, so give such directions half weight. Other frameworks of wellness (Te Whare Tapa Wha, the Social and Emotional Wellbeing domains, a Nation's own) take the same route through welprof and holbal, which accept any set of domains.

References

Health Canada, Assembly of First Nations (2015). First Nations Mental Wellness Continuum Framework. Ottawa: Health Canada. Summary report:
sac-isc.gc.ca/eng/1576093687903/1576093725971

See also

welprof, holbal.

Examples

# well-being, 2024 (table 41-10-0082-01): hope, and meaning and purpose
# (asked together); this table has no measure of belonging, so that direction
# is reported as missing
wb <- indiex("wellbeing")
mw <- mhcont(
  wb,
  "group",
  "indicator",
  "estimate",
  "lower",
  "upper",
  hope = "Always or often has a hopeful outlook",
  meaning = "Sense of meaning and purpose rating of 8, 9 or 10",
  purp = "Sense of meaning and purpose rating of 8, 9 or 10",
  qual = "quality"
)
mw
#> ╭── First Nations Mental Wellness Continuum: the four directions ────────╮
#> │   Groups      First Nations; Métis; Inuit                              │
#> │   Directions  hope, belonging, meaning, purpose                        │
#> │   Estimates   percent, from the published tables                       │
#> │                                                                        │
#> │   First Nations                                                        │
#> │   direction  estimate  95% CI          proxy                           │
#> │   ---------  --------  --------------  --------------                  │
#> │   hope          50.20  [45.90, 54.50]  yes                             │
#> │   belonging                            none published                  │
#> │   meaning       47.50  [43.40, 51.60]  yes (shared)                    │
#> │   purpose       47.50  [43.40, 51.60]  yes (shared)                    │
#> │                                                                        │
#> │   Métis                                                                │
#> │   direction  estimate  95% CI          proxy                           │
#> │   ---------  --------  --------------  --------------                  │
#> │   hope          52.30  [47.60, 57.00]  yes                             │
#> │   belonging                            none published                  │
#> │   meaning       51.60  [47.00, 56.20]  yes (shared)                    │
#> │   purpose       51.60  [47.00, 56.20]  yes (shared)                    │
#> │                                                                        │
#> │   Inuit                                                                │
#> │   direction  estimate  95% CI          proxy                           │
#> │   ---------  --------  --------------  --------------                  │
#> │   hope          54.40  [45.85, 62.95]  yes                             │
#> │   belonging                            none published                  │
#> │   meaning       50.50  [42.45, 58.55]  yes (shared)                    │
#> │   purpose       50.50  [42.45, 58.55]  yes (shared)                    │
#> │                                                                        │
#> │   No published proxy: belonging                                        │
#> │   -- reported as missing, never filled from another direction.         │
#> │   First Nations: highest hope (50.2), lowest meaning (47.5).           │
#> │   Métis: highest hope (52.3), lowest meaning (51.6).                   │
#> │   Inuit: highest hope (54.4), lowest meaning (50.5).                   │
#> │                                                                        │
#> │   Proxy for hope: Always or often has a hopeful outlook                │
#> │   Proxy for meaning: Sense of meaning and purpose rating of 8, 9 or 10 │
#> │   Proxy for purpose: Sense of meaning and purpose rating of 8, 9 or 10 │
#> │   Every level is a proxy: no survey table measures the directions as   │
#> │   the Framework defines them (Health Canada and AFN 2015).             │
#> │   yes (shared): one indicator serves two directions, counted for each. │
#> ╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
plot(mw)


# your own table: made-up percentages for two communities, with limits;
# one item stands for both meaning and purpose, and none for belonging
own <- data.frame(
  community = rep(c("Lakeside", "Riverbend"), each = 2),
  item = rep(c("Hopeful", "Life has meaning"), 2),
  pct = c(64, 70, 58, 75),
  lo = c(59, 65, 52, 70),
  hi = c(69, 75, 64, 80)
)
mhcont(own, "community", "item", "pct", "lo", "hi", hope = "Hopeful",
       meaning = "Life has meaning", purp = "Life has meaning")
